CDR-H3 突变 的变构效应调节保守的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RBD 靶向抗体的结合和中和
item.description: 未标记:进化 抗原 进化 继续削弱第一代单克隆抗体的活性,强调了识别刺突受体结合域 (RBD) 内保守特征的抗体的价值。作为面向广度的工程模型,我们评估了 RBD 导向的抗体 XG83,它具有 CDRH3 主导的互补位。利用 XG83-Wuhan RBD 晶体结构作为参考,我们将 MOE 丙氨酸扫描和残基扫描与 CDRH3 (A116-Y132) 集成,以识别化学上合理的替代物并测试与 Omicron BA.1 RBD 的相互作用。比较对接中以亲本 CDRH3 为中心的姿势比突变体 MuXG83 (-254.2) 具有更好的分数 (-280.18),并且 100 ns 分子动力学表明 MuXG83 稳定性较差(具有较高的 RMSD/RMSF 和较差的相互作用能)。针对 Omicron BA.1 RBD 的 ELISA 结果表明,XG83 的结合力比 MuXG83 强 40%;收敛仅发生在最高浓度,这与 SPR 研究以及 突变 增加解离的事实一致。根据这种结合间隙,BA.1 假病毒中和表明 XG83 比 MuXG83 更强大,表明 E118L/F130H CDR-H3 改变降低了针对 Omicron BA.1 的功能活性。这些结果意味着非表位 CDR-H3 残基对界面稳定性和构象动力学的变构影响会影响抗体性能。功能测试仅限于 Omicron BA.1;因此,需要更大规模的变异组研究来确定此类 突变 是否会影响抗体广度。我们的研究结果强调了优化互补位的结构引导方法,并表明 CDRH3 的非表位(潜在变构)变化在研究进展前的潜在发展和中和作用时也很重要。重要性:这项研究展示了 CDR-H3 中适度的变构特征如何控制中和效力和广度之间的微妙平衡,为 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗体工程做出了及时而重要的补充。本研究利用晶体学、丙氨酸扫描、残基扫描、对接、分子动力学以及实验 ELISA 和中和测定,为合理互补位优化提供了一个结构引导框架。调节长程稳定性而不仅仅是直接表位接触的 CDR-H3 残基的发现揭示了抗体设计中未被重视的方面,并解释了为什么一些改变改善了预期的相互作用但降低了功能性能。重要的是,野生型 XG83 和修饰后的 MuXG83 的比较显示了变构调节如何影响 Omicron 等变异体中抗体-抗原的相容性。这些发现阐明了保守的 RBD 识别,并为构建对病毒 进化 更具抵抗力的下一代治疗抗体提供了策略。

item.title: 疫苗接种 在预防 2019 年严重冠状病毒病中的关键作用:澳大利亚肾移植受者 队列研究 临床结果的观点

mRNA-1273 和 BNT162b2 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 二价加强剂 疫苗 在美国疗养院居民中的免疫原性比较。
item.description: 疗养院居民 (NHR) 仍然是最容易遭受 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染严重后果的人群之一。虽然 mRNA-1273(Spikevax,Moderna)和 BNT162b2(Comirnaty,Pfizer-BioNTech)疫苗 广泛用于该人群,但其免疫原性的比较数据,特别是在二价加强剂后,仍然有限。我们对接受 mRNA-1273 或 BNT162b2 二价 疫苗 的美国 NHR 进行了纵向免疫学评估。疫苗接种 后 10-30 天收集血清样本。使用基于 Luminex 珠的测定法测量抗尖峰 IgG 水平,并通过假病毒中和评估中和滴度。使用双边 Wilcoxon 秩和检验进行效价分布的比较分析。两个 疫苗 组均表现出对祖先武汉株和 Omicron BA.4/5 亚变体的强烈体液反应。mRNA -1273 和 BNT162b2 疫苗 制剂之间的刺突结合抗体水平和中和滴度相当。结论:mRNA-1273 和 BNT162b2 mRNA 疫苗 在 NHR 中都能引发类似的强大体液免疫,支持它们在加强策略中的互换使用。我们的研究结果强调了及时加强注射比精确产品选择对于保护这一高风险、免疫衰老人群的重要性。

item.description: 世界卫生组织(WHO)于2026年8月6日发布了全球风险评估,重点关注严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及其变种,包括JN.1、BA.2.86和Omicron。该文件强调了与大流行相关的持续风险,并强调需要持续监测和应对。尽管世卫组织积极参与风险评估并呼吁采取紧急行动遏制刚果民主共和国的埃博拉病毒 暴发,但该报告并未提供 暴发 的具体病例或死亡人数。该评估是管理该病毒对全球健康影响的更广泛努力的一部分,没有提及已解决的不确定性或大流行本身的当前状态更新。

item.title: COVID-19 dashboard
item.description: The WHO COVID-19 dashboard provides a global summary of confirmed SARS-CoV-2 cases and deaths, with data collected from countries, territories, and areas. It includes information on case definitions, testing strategies, and reporting practices, which vary by region. The dashboard has been updated since March 2020, with weekly data from July 2023 onwards. Data is subject to continuous verification and may change due to retrospective updates or shifts in reporting standards. WHO acknowledges that case detection, testing, and reporting practices differ globally, which can lead to under or overestimation of true case and death counts. Additionally, some countries have stopped reporting or changed their reporting frequency, which may affect the completeness of the data. The dashboard serves as a tool for monitoring the pandemic's spread and impact, but it is important to note that the data reflects official reports and may not capture all cases or deaths accurately.

item.title: Study finds COVID-19 can reactivate dormant viruses - American Hospital Association
item.description: A study published by the American Hospital Association (AHA) on August 7, 2026, suggests that COVID-19 may have the ability to reactivate dormant viruses. This finding is based on research conducted by the AHA, which highlights a potential risk associated with the virus. However, the evidence does not provide specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers. The study is reported as a research outcome, and no detailed investigation or response measures are outlined. The AHA emphasizes the importance of understanding such interactions to better manage the health impacts of the virus. The findings are part of broader discussions on healthcare cybersecurity and community health initiatives, but they do not constitute an outbreak or confirmed event. The study's implications are noted, but further research or confirmation is needed to fully understand the extent of this phenomenon.

item.title: COVID-19 - Encyclopedia Britannica
item.description: The article from Encyclopedia Britannica, published on August 6, 2026, provides an overview of SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights that the virus was first detected in Wuhan, China, in 2019 and quickly spread globally, leading to a multiyear pandemic with millions of deaths. The piece outlines the primary transmission routes, such as respiratory droplets and contaminated surfaces, and describes the symptoms of the disease, including fever, cough, and shortness of breath. It also notes the long-term effects on survivors, particularly those who required mechanical ventilation, and mentions the development of vaccines and treatments like remdesivir and monoclonal antibodies. The article emphasizes the impact of the pandemic on society, including the shift to remote work and education. However, it does not provide specific case counts, death counts, or details about investigations into the virus's origin or spread.

item.title: Severe COVID-19 reactivates dormant viruses and may leave a lasting viral signature - News-Medical
item.description: A Nature study of 1,154 unvaccinated U.S. patients hospitalized for COVID-19 between May 2020 and March 2021 reports that severe SARS-CoV-2 infection can reactivate dormant chronic viruses—including Anelloviridae and Herpesviridae—in people without overt immunosuppression. Persistent Anelloviridae activity during convalescence correlated with long COVID characterized by physical deficits, and viral reactivation patterns tracked disease severity. Critically ill patients with cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, or herpes simplex virus transcripts had higher one-year mortality, while Anelloviridae loads were elevated in older adults and those with prior organ transplant, myocardial infarction, shock, ICU care, or immunosuppression. The authors suggest quantitative PCR monitoring could aid prognostication, but emphasize that standardized clinical protocols and a full understanding of immune consequences are still lacking.

item.title: COVID-19 Reactivates Dormant Viruses, Offering New Clues to Long COVID - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News
item.description: 《遗传工程与生物技术新闻》于 2026 年 8 月 5 日发表的文章讨论了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 与休眠病毒重新激活之间的潜在联系,这可能为 长新冠 提供新的见解。然而,证据并未具体说明事件的确切日期、地点或受影响的人群。它还不包括详细的病例数、死亡数或暴露人数。研究结果作为假设而不是证实的结果提出,并且该文章是联合摘要,这意味着完整的原始文章正文无法供审查。文章中提到的研究表明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 可以重新激活其他病毒,可能导致某些个体出现长期症状。这是了解病毒长期影响的更广泛研究工作的一部分,但证据中没有说明明确的风险水平或应对措施。

item.title: 一种鲜为人知的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 蛋白可能为 长新冠 症状提供线索 - UCLA Health
item.description: A new UCLA study published on August 5, 2026, highlights the role of the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein in long COVID symptoms. Researchers discovered that this structural protein, less known than the spike protein, can amplify inflammatory signals in macrophages and weaken blood-vessel barriers in the heart, potentially contributing to cardiac complications. The study, conducted using engineered macrophages and stem cell-based models, suggests that the nucleocapsid protein may be a target for future therapies aimed at preventing severe COVID-19 and its lingering aftereffects. The findings are preliminary, and further research is needed to fully understand the implications. The research team, led by virologist Melody Li, is exploring how this protein interacts with the immune system, noting that coronaviruses often encode proteins that suppress antiviral defenses. The study underscores the importance of continued research into SARS-CoV-2 to improve patient care, especially for those with limited treatment options due to immunocompromised conditions.

item.title: RF.5 Omicron 变种与浦​​那的新冠病毒有关 - 印度时报
item.description: 《印度时报》于 2026 年 8 月 8 日报道,RF.5 Omicron 变种与印度浦那的新冠病毒感染有关。CSIR 国家化学实验室 (NCL) 的废水 监测 表明自 2026 年 7 月第一周以来病毒载量有所上升。州卫生部门确认 RF.5 是浦那目前流行的菌株。尽管在印度多个邦(包括马哈拉施特拉邦、德里、卡纳塔克邦等)的样本中都检测到了该变种,但没有迹象表明该病毒的行为发生了重大变化。卫生部门指出,目前的疫情似乎较轻,入院人数没有显着增加。对该变体的详细研究正在进行中,并对包括废水样本在内的 24 个样本进行基因组测序,以进一步评估循环变体。国家病毒学研究所已向政府提交了调查结果,预计很快就会有结果。

item.title: Cardiologists share vaccine recommendations for heart patients: Flu, COVID-19 and more - Cardiovascular Business
item.description: On August 6, 2026, cardiologists shared vaccine recommendations for heart patients, emphasizing the importance of Flu and COVID-19 vaccinations. The American College of Cardiology issued updated guidance highlighting that patients with a history of cardiovascular disease should prioritize vaccination. The report does not provide specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers, and the risk level is not explicitly stated. The guidance is considered preliminary and based on expert recommendations. No investigation or testing status is mentioned, and the information is presented as part of ongoing discussions about cardiovascular health and pandemic-related care. The report is a general guidance piece and does not indicate any confirmed or suspected outbreaks related to SARS-CoV-2.

item.title: What we’ve learned about Covid-19 since the pandemic - CNN
item.description: This article, published by CNN on August 4, 2026, discusses the evolving understanding of SARS-CoV-2 since the pandemic began. It highlights the effectiveness of vaccines in preventing severe disease, hospitalization, and death, with data showing that vaccinated individuals had significantly lower hospitalization rates than unvaccinated ones. The CDC reports that unvaccinated adults were 12 times more likely to be hospitalized with Covid-19. Nearly 1,700 children died from the virus between 2020 and 2023, with hospitalization rates among children consistently above 1 out of every 1,000. The article also mentions political debates and legal actions, including the HHS rejecting a CDC study for publication in its own journal and the FDA imposing strict limits on the Johnson & Johnson vaccine due to rare adverse events. The CDC continues to monitor vaccine safety and recommends updated vaccines for all ages 6 months and older.
